requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.references.outline_comments`. I did not request any implementation source, because the supplied tests were enough to decide.

**Run formation (consecutive lines, no other source between them).**
- `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next` asserts that two consecutive `//` lines both go to `fn[b]`.
- The python case in `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` does the same with "lead one" and "lead two".
- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` shows a blank line ending a run. "// before third", then a blank line, then `fn third` still belongs to `fn[third]`. The "floating" comment, which is separated from the following `mod m`, belongs to `mod[m]`, so blank lines separate runs as the text implies.
- In `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node`, "after a" is a trailing comment. The next line's "before b" is asserted to belong to `fn[b]`, so a trailing comment does not merge with the following comment line.

**A comment after other source on its line (including another comment) forms its own run and belongs to the innermost node containing that line.**
- `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` covers trailing comments after `fn a() {}`, after a statement inside `fn b`, after the closing `}` of `fn b`, and after the closing `}` of `mod m`. It asserts the owners `mod[m]/fn[a]`, `mod[m]/fn[b]` and `mod[m]`.
- `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers a comment after another comment (`/* first */ /* second */`). "first" goes to `fn[b]` and "second" goes to the root, because no node contains that line.
- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` checks `fn second() {} // trailing second` and the `innermost_at_line` result.

**Other runs: next node starting after the run within the smallest containing node, else the container, which is the root at top level.**
- Next node: `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next` and "above inner" in `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container`.
- Container when no node follows inside a `mod`: `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and "alone in m".
- Root at top level: `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` and "final".
- The same cases are repeated for Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown in `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language`. The YAML-specific `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` and the repository-level `workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows` add coverage there.

**Markdown profile.**
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` asserts that only the block comment is recorded. It asserts the inline `<!-- inline -->` lies in no comment range and that the line's owner is a `paragraph`. It also asserts that the block comment goes to `section[H]/section[Sub]`.

**Rust inner doc comments bound to their container.**
- `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` covers `//!` and `/*!` at file level, both owned by the root.
- "Module docs" in `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` shows `//!` inside `mod m` belongs to `mod[m]`, not to the following `fn inner`.
- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` shows `//!` before `fn after_inner_doc` does not cover that function.

**A reference in a comment counts for the owning node.**
- This obligation is delegated to the cited `rust_item_coverage` and `authoring_inputs`. It is still exercised by `rust_item_coverage`'s test, by `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes`, by `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run`, and by the search tests in `src/authoring/tools.rs` and `crates/habeas-sdk/src/structural.rs`. These tests assert on the owner.

I found no named boundary or failure case without a test that asserts its outcome. All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
